thesisQuality.note: Essential phosphate/potash demand and global customer reach support durable utility, while commodity/input economics limit moat quality.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 revenue was $2.8B and adjusted EBITDA $407M, but GAAP operating loss was $36M and net loss $273M amid elevated sulfur costs.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current market capitalization is about $7.5B after a material one-year share-price decline, but depressed earnings make simple P/E support weak; valuation is balanced rather than clearly cheap.

catalystScore.note: Lower 2026 capex and portfolio rationalization can improve cash economics, but timing of sulfur normalization and phosphate recovery is uncertain.

governancePower.note: Proxy documents stock-ownership requirements and management has taken explicit asset/capex actions tied to returns; CEO ownership remained below stated guideline at year-end 2025, tempering alignment.

alignment2036.note: Phosphate and potash are essential agricultural nutrients serving food-system productivity across more than 40 countries.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Potash, phosphates, Brazilian distribution and biosciences create several agricultural demand channels, but they remain correlated to crop economics.

bottleneckControl.note: Mosaic controls substantial nutrient production assets, but Q2 sulfur pricing and Brazilian idling show critical feedstock economics can shift the bottleneck away from owned capacity.

scenarioRobustness.note: Food nutrient demand is durable, yet profitability remains exposed to fertilizer prices, crop economics and sulfur/input cycles.

substitutionResilience.note: Phosphorus and potassium are agronomically necessary nutrients, though application intensity and product sourcing can change.

supplyChainResilience.note: Global production footprint provides some diversification, but sulfur exposure was severe enough to idle Brazilian operations and Q3 sulfur contracts settled at $705/long ton.

pricingPower.note: Essentiality supports demand but Q2 losses and sulfur-driven curtailments show limited ability to consistently pass input shocks through at attractive margins.

risk.note: Commodity cyclicality, sulfur/feedstock inflation and asset-utilization pressure are material; Q2 GAAP loss and Brazilian idling provide direct evidence.

confidence.note: Recent SEC earnings evidence, proxy governance evidence, issuer operating updates and independent current market data cover all components, while detailed long-run unit economics and current fertilizer spot economics remain incomplete.

thesis: Mosaic owns strategically relevant fertilizer capacity tied to durable food-system needs, but current underwriting is constrained by commodity cyclicality and unusually high sulfur/input costs.
keyRisk: Persistent sulfur and fertilizer-cycle pressure can keep phosphate assets underutilized and suppress cash returns despite durable nutrient demand.
nextCatalyst: Evidence of sulfur-cost normalization, improved phosphate margins/utilization, or further portfolio/capex discipline in the next reported quarter.
